correctness.rationale: For every r the composition expansion gives universal colored alternating chains. A missing interval bridge is separated by the explicitly constructed upset U=up((S∩T)∩up s1); a bridge forces the last point of every chain into U. For 2r>height, adjacent equality forces a common-color bridge; disjoint odd/even colors along a maximal chain give an extremal bad path for r=floor(h/2). If one-step product is a nucleus, its idempotence forces equality with the eventual intersection nucleus. The package verifier exhaustively checks all 242 labeled posets on 1..4 points and all 57,332 ordered nucleus pairs; finite checks support, but do not substitute for, the general proof.

value.rationale: Computing the join of two closure modalities is natural in locale/Heyting algebra semantics, and generic reflection gives no sharp finite iteration count. This theorem recovers a concrete exact interval characterization and proves the optimal height-based bound for all finite posets; its extremal chain constructions prevent improvement from height alone. It is more than a title change, fixed-value evaluation, or a routine special case of known nucleus representation.
